* Cell viability assays

DESCRIPTION:
Part 4 Final Data Analysis and Report

In a preceding pilot project, we demonstrated that TWIK-1 currents can be expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In this context, we tested various TWIK-1 mutations and buffer conditions for current recordings. Building on these results, the present follow-up project aims to establish a robust screening assay using the TWIK -1 triple mutant and a rubidium-containing recording buffer. The assay will be implemented on the high-throughput HiClamp instrument to screen a library of 500 compounds. All measurements will be performed at a single test potential. To achieve this, both technical optimization and standardized laboratory workflows will be required to ensure reliable and reproducible performance at scale.

PRODUCT_VARIANT_NAME: Polycystic Kidney Disease - PKD1 - Prevention/Screening/FSK (16 test articles, 2 conc each)
PRODUCT_NAME: Polycystic Kidney Disease - PKD1 - Prevention/Screening/FSK (16 test articles, 2 conc each)
DESCRIPTION:
Client test articles are evaluated for their ability to prevent the formation of cysts in the 3D Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) Translational Cell Models platform. The 3D PKD Prevention assay paradigm mimicks early-stage PKD where the test articles will be added to the culture media shortly after seeding. Cell number will be approximated by CellTiter-Glo® and Cyst metrics (Cyst Number and Total Cyst Area) will be measured by utilizing an AI-driven image analysis platform. Two (2) concentration points will need to be selected per test article. The cells used in this assay are primary cells derived from human PKD patient kidney tissue harboring a PKD1 mutation. Ricolinostat (CAS No. 1316214-52-4) will be used as a postive control, and Forskolin (CAS No. 66575-29-9) will be used as stimulus to accentuate cyst growth.

This assay is often paired with the LDH Cytotoxicity Assay (TCM0112).

Note: please refer to TCMCUSPKD001 when requesting a custom quote online or email PanlabsClientServices@eurofins.com to inquire about other assay paradigms and custom PKD assays.

* AlphaScreen
* Enzyme/reporter assays
* Cell viability assays

PRODUCT_NAME: Polycystic Kidney Disease - PKD1 - Prevention/Screening/AVP (16 test articles, 2 conc each)
DESCRIPTION:
Client test articles are evaluated for their ability to prevent the formation of cysts in the 3D Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) Translational Cell Models platform. The 3D PKD Prevention assay paradigm mimicks early-stage PKD where the test articles will be added to the culture media shortly after seeding. Cell number will be approximated by CellTiter-Glo® and Cyst metrics (Cyst Number and Total Cyst Area) will be measured by utilizing an AI-driven image analysis platform. Two (2) concentration points will need to be selected per test article. The cells used in this assay are primary cells derived from human PKD patient kidney tissue harboring a PKD1 mutation. Ricolinostat (CAS No. 1316214-52-4) will be used as a postive control, and Arginine Vasopressin (AVP) (CAS No. 113-79-1) will be used as stimulus to accentuate cyst growth.

This assay is often paired with the LDH Cytotoxicity Assay (TCM0112).

Note: please refer to TCMCUSPKD001 when requesting a custom quote online or email PanlabsClientServices@eurofins.com to inquire about other assay paradigms and custom PKD assays.

Screening of the Drugs for the Anti-microtubule or Anti-tubulin Activity: 
Drug-induced inhibition of the assembly of the mammalian microtubule protein or tubulin or tubulin isotypes is measured to assess the potency of the drug. From this test, one should be able to identify those drugs from a given library, which are active against microtubules, tubulin or one of its isoforms. 
Microtubule Protein (5 mg/ml) or Tubulin Protein (1 mg/ml) will be polymerized in the presence/absence of the test-compound and the polymerization will be followed by turbidimetry (change in absorbance at 340 nm). Total amount of the polymers in the steady state (where microtubule polymers are in equilibrium with the free tubulin), formed in the presence or absence of the test- compound, will be compared. All the experiments will be run in duplicate.

Result-format for Tests:
(1) The ORIGINAL DA340 values of control samples (in the absence of the test- compound).
(2) The ORIGINAL DA340 values of test samples (in the presence of the test- compound).
(3) The percent inhibition/stimulation of microtubule polymerization by the test- compound.

This basic screening utilizes drug-induced inhibition of the assembly of the mammalian MTs (mixture of tubulin and MAPs) to assess the potency of the drug. Unless specified, we will test the drugs at 1 and 100 mM concentrations. From this test, one should be able to identify those drugs from a given library, which are active against at least one of the constituents of microtubules (tubulin or one of the MAPs).
PRICE: $90 per compound 

Test 2: Anti-tubulin (MAP-free) Activity of test- compounds:
Our high thorough-put screening utilizes the drug-induced inhibition of polymerization of the purified mammalian tubulin (MAP-free), to assess the potency of the lead compound. Unless specified, we will test the drugs at 1 and 100 mM concentrations. The results from this screening can resolve whether or not the anti-mitotic activity of the compounds will arise from their interaction with tubulin.
PRICE: $125 per compound

PRICE: $250 per compound

From this test, one should be able to appraise the potency of a given drug relative to other drugs in the same library or to those reported in literature.

DESCRIPTION:
Part 3  screening a library of 500 compounds

In a preceding pilot project, we demonstrated that TWIK-1 currents can be expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In this context, we tested various TWIK-1 mutations and buffer conditions for current recordings. Building on these results, the present follow-up project aims to establish a robust screening assay using the TWIK -1 triple mutant and a rubidium-containing recording buffer. The assay will be implemented on the high-throughput HiClamp instrument to screen a library of 500 compounds. All measurements will be performed at a single test potential. To achieve this, both technical optimization and standardized laboratory workflows will be required to ensure reliable and reproducible performance at scale.

DESCRIPTION:
Client test articles are evaluated for their ability to prevent the formation of cysts in the 3D Polycystic Kidney Disease (PKD) Translational Cell Models platform. The 3D PKD Prevention assay paradigm mimicks early-stage PKD where the test articles will be added to the culture media shortly after seeding. Cell number will be approximated by CellTiter-Glo® and Cyst metrics (Cyst Number and Total Cyst Area) will be measured by utilizing an AI-driven image analysis platform. Two (2) concentration points will need to be selected per test article. The cells used in this assay are primary cells derived from human PKD patient kidney tissue harboring a PKD1 mutation. Ricolinostat (CAS No. 1316214-52-4) will be used as a postive control.

This assay is often paired with the LDH Cytotoxicity Assay (TCM0112).

Note: please refer to TCMCUSPKD001 when requesting a custom quote online or email PanlabsClientServices@eurofins.com to inquire about other assay paradigms and custom PKD assays.

DESCRIPTION: The HERG potassium channel is a major molecular component of the delayed rectifier current (IKr) underlying cardiac repolarization. Due to either genetic defects in its pore-forming subunit or adverse drug effects, decreased HERG activity prolongs the QT interval and can lead to the potentially lethal ventricular arrhythmia Torsades de pointes. The implication of (IKr) in cardiac arrhythmias and in anti-arrhythmic/pro-arrhythmic actions of drugs has driven intensive research interests in its structure-function relationship, the linkage between LQT-associated mutations and changes in channel function, and the mechanism of drug actions.

DESCRIPTION:
Part 2 Assay development for TWIK-1 Screening on HiClamp, as described above, complete package
In a preceding pilot project, we demonstrated that TWIK-1 currents can be expressed in Xenopus oocytes. In this context, we tested various TWIK-1 mutations and buffer conditions for current recordings. Building on these results, the present follow-up project aims to establish a robust screening assay using the TWIK -1 triple mutant and a rubidium-containing recording buffer. The assay will be implemented on the high-throughput HiClamp instrument to screen a library of 500 compounds. All measurements will be performed at a single test potential. To achieve this, both technical optimization and standardized laboratory workflows will be required to ensure reliable and reproducible performance at scale.
